## The G2G Model

The **Grassia(II)-Geometric (G2G)** model is a discrete-time survival model that
accounts for unobserved heterogeneity across subjects (Fader and Hardie, 1997).
Each subject has a latent event rate $\lambda$ drawn from a Gamma
distribution, which corresponds to a baseline per-period event probability
$p_0$:

$$\lambda \sim \text{Gamma}(r,\, \alpha), \qquad p_0 = 1 - e^{-\lambda}$$

Covariates shift this baseline propensity through a log-linear link. For a
subject with covariate vector **x**, the cumulative covariate effect at period
*t* is $C(t) = t \cdot \exp(\mathbf{x}'\boldsymbol{\beta})$, and the survivor
function is:

$$S(t) = \left(1 + \frac{C(t)}{\alpha}\right)^{-r}$$

The parameters **r** (shape) and **alpha** (rate) characterize the population
distribution of baseline propensity; **beta** is a vector of covariate
log-hazard coefficients.

## Setup

```{r load-packages}
library(G2Gcov)
library(survival)
```

## Example Data: Veteran Lung Cancer Trial

We use the `veteran` dataset from the `survival` package (Kalbfleisch and
Prentice, 1980), a randomized trial of two treatments for lung cancer with
137 patients.

```{r load-data}
# veteran is lazy-loaded in the survival package; accessible directly
vet <- survival::veteran

# Add a unique subject ID (required by the visualization functions)
vet$id <- seq_len(nrow(vet))

head(vet[, c("id", "time", "status", "age", "karno")])
```

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `time`   | Survival time (days) |
| `status` | 1 = death, 0 = censored |
| `age`    | Age in years |
| `karno`  | Karnofsky performance score (0–100; higher is better) |

```{r data-summary}
cat("Subjects:", nrow(vet), "\n")
cat("Events:  ", sum(vet$status), "\n")
cat("Censored:", sum(1 - vet$status), "\n")
```

## Fitting the Model

`G2G_static_MLE()` accepts a standard `Surv()` formula. Internally it
maximizes the G2G log-likelihood via BFGS and returns parameter estimates,
standard errors, and 95% confidence intervals.

```{r fit-model}
fit <- G2G_static_MLE(
  Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno,
  data = vet
)

cat("Convergence code:", fit$convergence,
    ifelse(fit$convergence == 0, "(converged)", "(check starting values)"), "\n")
cat("Negative log-likelihood:", round(fit$value, 2), "\n")
```

## Parameter Estimates

```{r results-table}
results <- data.frame(
  Parameter = names(fit$par),
  Estimate  = fit$par,
  SE        = fit$par_stderr,
  CI_Lower  = fit$par_lower,
  CI_Upper  = fit$par_upper,
  row.names = NULL
)

knitr::kable(
  results,
  digits    = 3,
  col.names = c("Parameter", "Estimate", "Std. Error",
                "Lower 95% CI", "Upper 95% CI"),
  caption   = "G2G parameter estimates -- veteran data"
)
```

**Interpreting the estimates:**

- **r (shape)** and **alpha (rate)** define the Gamma distribution of the
  baseline event rate $\lambda$. The population mean of the baseline
  per-period event probability is
  $1 - (\alpha / (\alpha + 1))^r = `r round(1 - (fit$par[2] / (fit$par[2] + 1))^fit$par[1], 3)`$.
- Covariate coefficients are on the log-hazard scale. Positive values
  increase the hazard (shorter survival); negative values decrease it.

**Hazard ratios** are obtained by exponentiating covariate coefficients:

```{r hazard-ratios}
coef_idx <- seq_along(fit$par)[-(1:2)]
hr_df <- data.frame(
  Covariate   = names(fit$par)[coef_idx],
  Coefficient = fit$par[coef_idx],
  HR          = exp(fit$par[coef_idx]),
  row.names   = NULL
)
knitr::kable(
  hr_df,
  digits    = 3,
  col.names = c("Covariate", "Coefficient", "Hazard Ratio"),
  caption   = "Covariate hazard ratios"
)
```

A hazard ratio below 1 indicates a protective effect. Higher Karnofsky score
(better functional status) is associated with reduced hazard, consistent with
clinical expectation.

## Baseline Propensity Distribution

`plot_p0()` plots the distribution of the baseline per-period event
probability $p_0 = 1 - e^{-\lambda}$ implied by the fitted Gamma
distribution. The shaded region covers the central 90% of the distribution;
the solid vertical line marks the mean and the dashed line the mode.

```{r plot-p0, fig.cap = "Distribution of the baseline per-period event probability"}
plot_p0(fit)
```

A wide distribution indicates substantial unobserved heterogeneity; a narrow
distribution suggests a relatively homogeneous population.


## Survivor Curve

`plot_survival_insample_g2g()` plots the model-implied survivor function
S(t) over the training data. Each period's model retention is averaged over
the subjects still at risk, and these rates are chained together in the same
way as a Kaplan-Meier curve.

```{r plot-survival, fig.cap = "In-sample G2G survivor curve"}
plot_survival_insample_g2g(
  fo         = Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno,
  train      = vet,
  subject    = "id",
  model_type = "static"
)
```

## Model Diagnostics

```{r diagnostics}
# AIC: 2k - 2 * log-likelihood
k   <- length(fit$par)
aic <- 2 * k + 2 * fit$value
cat("Parameters:", k, "\n")
cat("AIC:       ", round(aic, 2), "\n")

# Standard errors (NA when Hessian is singular)
if (anyNA(fit$par_stderr)) {
  cat("Note: some standard errors are NA (near-singular Hessian).\n")
} else {
  cat("All standard errors are finite.\n")
}
```
